newsitem.title: USA: LPC - Campbell taps banks to fund buyback.
newsitem.headline: LPC - Campbell taps banks to fund buyback.

text.p: NEW YORK, Sept 13 (LPC) - J.P. Morgan and Co Inc and Chase Manhattan Corp are leading a $2.5 billion bank loan backing Campbell Soup Co's repurchase of 18 million shares for between $69 and $80 a share, market sources said.
The deal is split between a $1.0 billion, 364-day facility and a $1.5 billion, five-year revolver, sources said.
Pricing on the shorter tranche starts at 12 basis points over the London Inter-Bank Offered Rate (LIBOR) for drawn amounts, plus a three-basis-point annual fee, bankers said.
On the longer tranche of the loan, pricing is 9.5 basis points over LIBOR for drawn amounts, plus a 5.5-basis-point annual fee, bankers added.
If the company's debt rating drops below AA-minus from Standard and Poor's or Aa3 by Moodys Investors Service, pricing would rise slightly, according to bankers.
Campbell's senior unsecured debt is presently rated AA by S&P and is on CreditWatch with negative implications, according to the rating agency.
The credit also will be used for general corporate purposes and acquisitions, bankers said.
